title: Time Off and Happiness Across Countries: Long-Run Institutional Change, Comparative Well-Being Panels, and Policy-Reform Evidence
domain: labor economics / subjective well-being / comparative social policy / causal inference
summary: Expanded cross-national study of how paid annual leave, weekly rest, public holidays and realized working time evolved over the long twentieth century and early twenty-first century, linked to multi-source subjective well-being evidence from the postwar era onward. The completed eight-event/Israel Life Ladder study is preserved as Pilot-0, a narrow causal-identification module rather than the whole project.
